prize_parts.citation: for introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory and thereby transforming the analysis of exporting, reallocation and the gains from trade

statement.case_for: Firm heterogeneity and selection is a discovery with a clear mechanism: trade liberalisation reallocates activity toward more productive firms, which adds a channel for the gains from trade beyond the representative-firm models. The framework has also held up empirically. Exporter premia, selection into exporting and FDI-versus-export choices have been tested on firm-level microdata for more than two decades, and the model is now the standard foundation for trade and productivity analysis. This is the combination of theory and data that I value most: a model built to explain firm-level facts, then confirmed on new data. Attribution is clean at two names, with Melitz (2003) as the originating model and Helpman as the central companion through the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple work on exporting versus FDI and through his broader trade-structure agenda. Redding's quantitative and spatial work builds on the core insight and is not needed for the discovery. After nearly two decades without a prize in trade (last recognised in 2008), the timing is favourable and maturity is not in question.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution beyond the ballot's named group. Bernard and Jensen documented the exporter facts, and Eaton and Kortum built a parallel heterogeneous-producer framework. A two-name award built on the Melitz model could be read as understating them. Helpman also appears in B007 (with Grossman), so the Committee must decide which body of his work it is honouring. Quantitative welfare conclusions from heterogeneous-firm models are also sensitive to functional-form assumptions, such as the Pareto productivity distribution, and the gains-from-trade results are partly model-dependent. I rely on general knowledge of the literature for these credit shares and have not verified them against sources.

responses.point: Friberg ranks Kiyotaki-Moore (B043) first. The collateral-constraint credit-cycle mechanism is cleanly attributable to the two originators, the Gertler-Gilchrist financial-accelerator strand is distinct, and the mechanism itself has not yet been recognised, even though related work was honoured in 2022.
responses.response: I agree on attribution and now prefer the pair, so I no longer propose adding Gertler. My opening ranking of B043 as second included him, but a separate strand overlapping with the Bernanke recognition and with B021 weakens the claim for a third name. I still keep B012 ahead. The firm-heterogeneity discovery has a more extensive record of direct microdata confirmation, while the identification of collateral-driven amplification remains debated, as several colleagues and I have noted. B043 is a serious alternative, and I would support it if the Committee concludes that financial-friction macro has the stronger claim.

responses.point: Andersson ranks the Grossman-Helpman political economy of trade protection (B007) first. He argues that the pair are clear originators of a tractable model of lobbying and tariffs, that the two-person attribution is clean, and that trade has been recognised only indirectly since Krugman. He also notes that empirical support for the lobbying model is mixed.
responses.response: I accept that the attribution is cleaner for B007 than for almost any other ballot. I still rank it behind B012 on scope and confirmation. The Melitz framework changed the standard unit of analysis in trade and has been tested on firm data throughout, whereas Protection for Sale is narrower and, as Andersson himself says, has mixed empirical support. Helpman's presence in both candidacies argues for one coherent trade recognition rather than two. Because the heterogeneous-firm work is more widely used as a foundation, I would frame a trade prize around B012 and not pair Helpman with Grossman.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B022 first. The task framework and the China-shock evidence changed how economists and policymakers understand technology, trade and distributional adjustment, and the China-shock trio of Autor, Dorn and Hanson is a clean attribution. She concedes that the size and persistence of the effects are still contested.
responses.response: The importance and credibility of the China-shock design are real, and the attribution to Autor, Dorn and Hanson is defensible. My reservations are about maturity and scope. The persistence and magnitude of the effects are still being revised, and the task framework has important contributors outside the credited set, notably Acemoglu, Levy and Murnane, which creates overlap with the 2024 recognition. The firm-heterogeneity framework has had more time to be confirmed and refined, and its core insight has not been revised by later work. I therefore keep B022 as an alternative, not my preferred part, but I would not oppose it. It may be the better choice if the Committee weights societal significance more heavily than conceptual foundation.

uncertainties: How the Committee should treat Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, whose parallel empirical and theoretical contributions are not on the ballot but could affect how fairly a two-name award reflects the discovery.
Whether Helpman's recognition should be framed around firm heterogeneity (B012) or the Grossman-Helpman political-economy work (B007), or both.
Whether the welfare conclusions of heterogeneous-firm models are robust enough to stand as the prize's core.
How much weight to give B043 versus B012 if the Committee prioritises macro-finance.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. My research is in corporate finance, and the profile lists no co-authorship or institutional tie to Helpman or Melitz. I disclose my adjunct professorship at Chicago Booth and my KVA vice-presidency, but neither is a specific connection to a candidate on the shortlist.
